purpose: Pre-freeze diagnostics; read-only, does not alter the pipeline.

cohort_in_sample.note: Colorado cohort, households>=100; in-sample r^2 for income-only OLS

cohort_income_only_cv.note: pooled_out_of_fold_predictive_R2 is what regression_metrics reports; it is 1 - SSE/SST on held-out predictions, NOT the squared Pearson r. For a single-feature OLS the in-sample R2 equals r^2; the predictive R2 differs and on this filtered Colorado cohort is much higher than the full-union r^2.

check1_eda_reconciliation.reconciliation: The two numbers are different quantities on different populations. EDA r=0.24 -> r^2=0.058 is the squared Pearson correlation on the full 1,161-code union with the raw target. The 0.48 figure is pooled out-of-fold predictive R2 of an income-only model on the 418-code Colorado households>=100 cohort. Restricting to Colorado and removing tiny-denominator rate artifacts strengthens the income-adoption relationship, and predictive R2 is not the squared correlation. Both numbers are correct for what they measure; neither is an error.

check2_nested_selection_audit.verdict: The winner MAE (picked as the min over candidates on their own outer-fold means) is compared to a fully nested procedure that selects the candidate INSIDE each outer-train block. The gap is the residual candidate-selection bias. A small gap means picking the best-of-k on outer scores barely inflates the reported number; we report the fully nested figure as the honest headline for the selection procedure.

check4_paired_folds.verdict: The two-feature model is NOT significantly better on paired folds; the ~0.4 MAE gap is within fold noise. It is selected for being as accurate while simpler and more consistent (lower fold std), not for a proven accuracy edge.
